summary: A design and its declared latency meet the trusted statement exactly when, for every (N, W, AccW) in range, they have all of the properties below. The last five are guarantees the design owes an environment that follows the protocol: after a reset is released, start is raised only while the design is idle, and A and B are held from start until done rises. Lean checks that, together, the properties say exactly what the statement says, nothing less and nothing more (the theorem statement_iff_properties).

properties.name: PARAMS_IN_RANGE
properties.text: The statement covers every matrix size N ≥ 1, entry width W ≥ 1 and accumulator width AccW ≥ 1, as long as both port widths, N·N·W and N·N·AccW bits, stay below 2^31: the parameters are 32-bit ints, and in that range a real SystemVerilog tool and Lean's model agree on every width and index. One proof covers all of them; the design is scored at N = 4, W = 8, AccW = 32.

properties.name: INTERFACE
properties.text: The module has exactly the input ports clk, rst, start (1 bit each), A and B (N·N·W bits each) and exactly the output ports done (1 bit) and C (N·N·AccW bits), with these widths, in this order. Nothing is missing and nothing is extra: an extra input could serve as a hidden mode pin, and the checker and the scoring tools drive and read the design by these names and widths. No two declarations of the module (ports or internal signals) share a name, so every port has exactly one declared width. Matrices are flat, row-major, least significant entry first: entry (i, k) of A is A[(i·N+k)·W +: W].

properties.name: CLOCK_DISCIPLINE
properties.text: The clock is the input clk: every register is clocked by it, no register has an asynchronous reset (rst is synchronous, read inside the clocked processes), and no logic reads clk as a data signal. Together these make one cycle of Lean's model exactly one rising edge of clk in the real circuit: a clock that is gated, derived from logic, tied off or never driven is ruled out. One consequence to know: the registers have to sit in the top module, because connecting clk to a child instance copies it as data.

properties.name: TERMINATES
properties.text: From every power-up state (every register and variable, 2-state ones included, holding some 0 or 1), whatever order the simulator picks for processes that are ready at the same moment (the schedule), and whatever known values the environment drives on the inputs, simulating the design completes: every clock cycle settles. A combinational loop that oscillates fails this, and so does a design the tools could not read. It is also what gives the guarantees below their teeth: they are about completed runs, and a design with no completed run would satisfy them without doing anything.

properties.name: LATENCY_AT_LEAST_ONE
properties.text: Besides the design, a submission declares its latency: the number of cycles it may take to answer a start, as a function of the parameters. It must be at least one cycle. The checker pins its value at the scoring point, and the score uses it (time = latency × clock period), so declaring a larger latency than needed only costs score.

properties.name: MOORE_OUTPUTS
properties.text: No combinational path leads from any input, rst included, to done and C: the outputs are functions of the registers only. The proof reads the outputs in the snapshot just after a clock edge, with that cycle's inputs still applied; on the wire the inputs change before the next edge. Without this rule an output that reads an input directly would be proved on one value and seen on another; an output gated by rst could hide a transaction's last value from a consumer when a reset follows (the clocked tasks' rule 1: no input reaches an output combinationally).

properties.name: NO_X_CREATING
properties.text: No construct of the design can make an unknown value out of known ones: no run-time / or % except by a nonzero constant, no ** that could be x, no run-time index that can leave its range, no slice beyond its operand, no bitwise or equality operator on operands of different widths, no x or z literal outside a casez/casex pattern. Together with the power-up rule, every value the design computes in Lean's model is then a known 0 or 1, so every if, case and ?: decides on a known value, where the hardware decides too (rule 3: no construct creates an unknown).

properties.name: DONE_KNOWN
properties.text: As long as the environment follows the protocol, done is a known bit, 0 or 1, in every cycle from the release of the reset on. The environment decides when to start the next transaction by watching done, so done must mean something in every cycle; never x.

properties.name: DONE_LOW_BEFORE_FIRST_START
properties.text: As long as the environment follows the protocol, done is 0 in every cycle after the release of the reset and before the first start. done = 1 claims a result, and before the first start there is none: a design that raises done too soon fails here, whatever C shows.

properties.name: DONE_WITHIN_LATENCY
properties.text: As long as the environment follows the protocol, after every start, done is 1 in some cycle at most lat cycles later, counting the cycle in which start is sampled as cycle 0. Finishing earlier is fine, and the number of cycles may depend on the data, as long as it never exceeds the declared latency.

properties.name: DONE_HELD
properties.text: As long as the environment follows the protocol, once done has been 1 after a start, it stays 1 in every cycle until the next start. The result does not vanish: the environment may read it at any time before it starts the next transaction.

properties.name: RESULT_IS_PRODUCT
properties.text: As long as the environment follows the protocol, in every cycle from the first done = 1 after a start until the next start, C holds the matrix product A·B of the operands driven when start was sampled. Entries of A and B are signed W-bit numbers, and each C[i][j] = Σ_k A[i][k]·B[k][j] is computed exactly and then wrapped to AccW bits (modulo 2^AccW, as a GPU accumulator does). Once done rises the environment may change A and B, so the design must keep the result, not recompute it from its inputs.

definitions.name: product
definitions.text: product N W AccW A B: the matrix product, each entry Σ_k A[i][k]·B[k][j] over signed W-bit entries, reduced modulo 2^AccW, packed flat and row-major.

definitions.name: dot
definitions.text: dot N W A B i j: the exact integer Σ_{k<N} A[i][k]·B[k][j].

definitions.name: entry
definitions.text: entry W x idx: entry idx of a flat vector of W-bit signed entries, as an integer.

definitions.name: TxTask.Rely
definitions.text: The environment's side of the protocol, up to a horizon: start and the operands are driven with known values in every cycle, start is 1 only while the design is idle, and the operands of a start are held until the cycle in which done first rises.

definitions.name: TxTask.Idle
definitions.text: The design is idle: every start since the release has already been answered by a cycle with done = 1.

definitions.name: Finished
definitions.text: Finished stim tr c1 s c: s is a start after the release c1, done has been 1 in some cycle from s to c, and there is no later start up to c. These are the cycles in which the result must be shown.

definitions.name: TxTask.Guar
definitions.text: The trusted guarantee, one conjunction; DONE_KNOWN, DONE_LOW_BEFORE_FIRST_START, DONE_WITHIN_LATENCY, DONE_HELD and RESULT_IS_PRODUCT are its parts.

definitions.name: Statement
definitions.text: The trusted challenge statement that these properties restate, part by part.

definitions.name: task
definitions.text: The task as data: the parameter range, the port names and widths, and the function of a transaction.

definitions.name: UnderProtocol
definitions.text: UnderProtocol d G: in every completed run from every power-up state on every known stimulus, from every release of the reset, up to every later cycle h before which the environment followed the protocol (the task's Rely), G holds up to h. Every guarantee is stated in this frame, so a protocol violation can only void claims about later cycles.

definitions.name: Released
definitions.text: Released rst stim c1 h: rst was 1 in the cycle before c1 and is 0 in every cycle from c1 up to h. Claims start at every release, so nothing may survive a reset.

definitions.name: TraceBit
definitions.text: TraceBit tr c n b: in cycle c the design shows the 1-bit signal n as the known bit b.

definitions.name: StimBit
definitions.text: StimBit stim c n b: in cycle c the environment drives the 1-bit input n with the known bit b.

definitions.name: ClockedBy
definitions.text: The trusted clock discipline that CLOCK_DISCIPLINE restates.

definitions.name: edgeClock
definitions.text: The clock of a clocked process (always_ff @(posedge c) and the like); none for any other process.

definitions.name: asyncReset
definitions.text: The asynchronous reset of a clocked process (the rn of posedge c or negedge rn), if it has one.

definitions.name: processDataNames
definitions.text: Every signal a process reads or writes as data: its body, or its assignment. The clock and reset in the event control do not count.

definitions.name: inputPorts
definitions.text: The design's input ports, each with its declared width, in declaration order.

definitions.name: outputPorts
definitions.text: The design's output ports, each with its declared width, in declaration order.

definitions.name: HoldAll
definitions.text: HoldAll st ports values: in the state st, every listed port holds its value as a known bit vector (no x, no z) of exactly the port's width.

definitions.name: ScheduleOracle
definitions.text: A legal schedule: the order in which the simulator runs the processes that are ready at the same moment. The statement quantifies over all of them.

definitions.name: Process2.isEdgePhase
definitions.text: True for the processes that run at the clock edge: always_ff, always @(posedge …) and asynchronous-reset blocks.

definitions.name: MooreOutDep
definitions.text: The trusted rule 1 that MOORE_OUTPUTS restates: a set of signals that holds every input port outside the exempt list (here the list is empty: every input port, rst included), is closed along every combinational dependency and holds no output port.

definitions.name: combDeps
definitions.text: The combinational dependencies of a design, by assignment: for each always_comb or continuous assign, every signal a write targets and every signal its value, its indices or an enclosing condition reads. A clocked process contributes none: its writes end a combinational path at the clock edge.

definitions.name: ModelsPU
definitions.text: ModelsPU d P: from every power-up state, under every schedule, on every known stimulus, every completed run of d satisfies P. It replaces the earlier statement's runs from Lean's own start state, where an unreset register is x: an unreset register is a 0 or 1 nobody knows, so the claims must hold for every value it can have.

definitions.name: PowerUp
definitions.text: PowerUp d st: st binds every declared signal of d, in declaration order, to a value of its declared width whose every bit is 0 or 1 (2-state declarations included, initializers ignored).

definitions.name: KnownStim
definitions.text: KnownStim d stim: every stimulus entry binds each input port it drives to a value of the port's width whose every bit is 0 or 1. An x on an input is a value the environment does not know; each of its resolutions is a known entry.

definitions.name: KnownEntry
definitions.text: KnownEntry d e: every input port the entry e binds holds a known value of its declared width.

definitions.name: sigWidth
definitions.text: The declared width of a signal (its first declaration's).

definitions.name: RunsAt
definitions.text: RunsAt d σ st0 stim tr: simulating d from the state st0 under the schedule σ on the stimulus stim completes, with the trace tr.

definitions.name: run2At
definitions.text: Lean's run of a design (ls-sv's run2: the same clock cycles and checks) started from a given state instead of its own start state.

definitions.name: TerminatesPU
definitions.text: The trusted termination conjunct that TERMINATES restates: from every power-up state, under every schedule, every known stimulus completes.

definitions.name: XSafe
definitions.text: The trusted rule 3 that NO_X_CREATING restates: every process passes the structural check xsafeB.

definitions.name: xsafeB
definitions.text: The structural check of rule 3, a Boolean function of the design's text and declared widths: every expression of every process has a rule-3 width (xsWidth), and every case pattern is an admitted expression or a casez/casex literal.

definitions.name: xsWidth
definitions.text: The width of an expression's value when no construct in it can create an x from known operands, and none otherwise: literals without x/z digits, declared signals, slices in range, run-time indices whose every value is in range, equal widths for bitwise and equality operators and for the two arms of ?:, and the operator rules of binW.

definitions.name: binW
definitions.text: Rule 3 at a binary operator: / and % only by a nonzero constant, ** with a signed exponent only on a nonzero constant base, &, |, ^, ==, !=, ==?, !=? only on equal widths; every other operator is known on known operands.
